evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the 10–15 minute timeframe or asked for a yes before diving into account lookup and probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep never asked 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' — jumped straight into confirming existing estimate details and logistics.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep stated 'my colleague already send you the quotation and that would be for 1300' — a price point mentioned, but no personalized range, no framing of why (size, services, prep level), no anchoring language ('typical for a home your size').
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: No mention of trip fees, overnight fees, packing materials, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, or 'not a guess' framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent; no pause held for customer reaction to price.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' — instead moved directly to 'Do you want me to reserve the movers and the truck for you on the 5th of November?' after stating a confirmation email would be sent, implying the booking was already made.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date (Nov 5), email address, and move addresses confirmed; missing phone number, arrival window, crew size, and crew notes about customer concerns. Partial credit.

top_strength: Zhang secured all four discovery basics cleanly (name, moving day, both locations, square footage, room counts, distances) and confirmed logistics details comprehensively before any pricing discussion.
coaching_note: This call skipped the entire 15-Minute Quote Call framework: no quid pro quo open, no 'Their Agenda' / concerns check, no pricing anchor or fee framing, no Two Promises, no final concerns check, and no explicit ask—Zhang inherited an existing quote and simply re-confirmed and booked it, which is not the script structure reps are trained on.
